private_notes.observations: No rate cards or hour allocations are available yet. Our fully loaded cost is $200 per hour, and demand depends on both our relative rate and overall panel rates.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that provides a meaningful margin. Use subsequent rate cards and allocated hours to estimate price sensitivity and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate exceeded both competitors’ $274 rates, yet we received 190 hours and earned $28,538. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how strongly allocation responds to price.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate modestly to test whether a narrower price gap increases hours enough to offset the lower margin. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making a larger change.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $350 to $340 increased allocated hours from 190 to 228 and quarterly profit from $28,538 to $31,861. Both competitors held at $274 in Q1 and Q2. The observed improvement supports testing a further reduction, though two quarters do not establish the allocation formula.
private_notes.plan: Set $310 for Q3 to test whether a substantially narrower gap to the competitors increases hours enough to improve profit. Compare resulting hours and profit against Q2 before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Competitors held at $274 in Q1–Q3. Cutting our rate from $350 to $310 increased allocated hours from 190 to 379 and quarterly profit from $28,538 to $41,713.
private_notes.plan: Test a rate close to competitors’ $274 to see whether additional hours outweigh the narrower margin. Compare Q4 profit and hours with Q3 before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: Competitors held at $274 throughout Q1–Q4. Reducing our rate from $310 to $280 increased allocated hours from 379 to 598 and quarterly profit from $41,713 to $47,822.
private_notes.plan: Test $267, modestly below both competitors. The observed response to price cuts suggests the additional hours may outweigh the smaller margin; compare Q5 profit with Q4 before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Competitors held at $274 in Q1–Q5. Profit was nearly identical at $280 ($47,822) and $267 ($47,710), suggesting the best rate lies between them.
private_notes.plan: Set $273, just below both competitors. Compare next quarter's hours and profit with Q4–Q5 before making further changes.

private_notes.observations: Competitors have held at $274 for six quarters. Our profit was highest at $273 ($48,038), with $267 and $280 producing slightly less.
private_notes.plan: Test $274, near the estimated profit-maximizing rate. Compare realized hours and profit with Q6 before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: With both competitors at $274 throughout, profits were highest at $274 ($48,045), narrowly above $273 ($48,038). Rates of $267 and $280 earned slightly less.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $274. The observed profit differences near this rate are small, so avoid reacting to minor quarterly variation; reassess if allocation or competing rates change.
